subject: Finova decision criteria — latency & deployment follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Finova — decision criteria recap + next steps

Hi Alejandro — great to meet today. Thanks for walking through Finova's priorities for the lending-product assistant. Per our discussion, I'm capturing the decision criteria and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of decision criteria we heard today:
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency target of <= 150ms for single-turn scoring (tight for interactive search flows).
- Cost: target token-based cost goal of <$0.003 per 1k tokens for production queries (looking for a 2-3x improvement vs current).
- Deployment mode: preference for Private (VPC) if SOC2 + data residency checks pass; Dedicated reserved capacity as fallback.
- SLA: firm uptime SLA expectations (99.9% for revenue-critical endpoints) + support turnaround for incident P1s within 1 hour.
- Security: SOC 2, audit logs, customer-managed KMS non-negotiable for pilot.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I attached a short SLOs & deployment options doc (PDF) — it maps our runtimes to the latency/cost tradeoffs we discussed. Please review the latency table on page 2.
2) If the latency target above is accurate, can you confirm whether the 150ms number is for requests of average length ~30 tokens or worst-case longer sequences? That will change the recommended model variant.
3) Can you introduce the procurement contact (Procurement Team) if procurement needs to be moved in next week?
4) We’ll draft a mutual action plan (MAP) for the pilot — I’ll share the first draft by Thursday.

If this looks right I’ll loop in Dev to outline the minimal telemetry and integration checklist for the pilot.

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Finova — decision criteria recap + next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the doc. Quick answers inline: 

- Latency: the 150ms is our target for the common-case (short form queries ~20-40 tokens). We understand longer context windows will push latency higher; still want to aim for 95th <= 200ms for those.
- Cost: the <$0.003/1k was aspirational; procurement will need a clearer breakdown vs current spend.
- Deployment: we prefer Private VPC for data residency, but procurement has asked for a Dedicated option cost comparison as part of their evaluation.
- SLA: 99.9% is what our product team needs; procurement will push for credit language in a contract instead of one-off exceptions.

Procurement contact is included here (procurement@finova.com). Maya from our product team will own technical evaluation and will coordinate security/compliance evidence requests.

Two asks for you: 
1) Can you confirm which Redwood model variants hit 95th <=150ms for 20-40 token queries on Dedicated vs Private (rough numbers are fine)?
2) Please add a simple cost-perqps and monthly reserved capacity estimate to the MAP so procurement has something to review.

Appreciate it — Alejandro
Alejandro Torres
Head of Product, Consumer Lending | Finova
alejandro.torres@finova.com

Quick technical note (adding to the thread for transparency):
- For 20-40 token single-turn inference, our benchmark (Dedicated, n1-standard GPUs, 16k KV) shows: Redwood-llama2-13b-quant (optimized) -> median 70ms, p95 ~140-160ms depending on batching. On Private VPC with equivalent GPU types the numbers are roughly +10-20ms overhead for networking & isolation, so p95 ~160-180ms.
- Recommended approach: pilot on Dedicated reserved capacity (to hit latency goals reliably) while we scope the security onboarding for Private. If procurement insists on Private comparison, we can provide a cost delta and timeline (Private typically adds 15-30% infra/Ops premium).
- For the MAP: reserve 4 GPUs for pilot (estimate 25 sustained p95 queries/sec with 8 concurrent model-workers), monthly cost estimate included in the MAP sheet.

I’ll update the MAP with the model variants and the cost-per-qps numbers by end of day.
